newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Investor disinterest sees Singapore shares weaker.
newsitem.headline: Investor disinterest sees Singapore shares weaker.

text.p: A lack of investor interest saw Singapore shares open weaker on Thursday.
"It's that sort of day again," said one local dealer. "The market's a little off and the volume's low."
At 0245 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index had dipped 5.55 points to 2,042.34, extending the downward drift that has been the main characteristic of the trading week so far.
Total market volume was a thin 32 million shares which saw early losers thrashing early gainers 136 to 48.
"There are no incentives to get the market going," another dealer said.
DBS Land retained a high profile after its 92 million share placement announcement on Tuesday and speculation about a possible bid for healthcare firm Parkway.
The counter topped early actives with 3.5 million units traded. It remained unchanged at Singapore $4.76.
OCBC Bank domestic and foreign tranches were diluted with the listing of bonus issue shares announced in March. OCBC stood at S$8.05, with the foreign tranche at S$15.30.
Thai telephone company Total Access Communications topped early gainers, up US$0.22 at US$4.90, but on low volume.
